steps.title: Definition
steps.body: Structure analysis examines how a text is organised - the order of ideas, paragraphing, sentence variety, and narrative techniques used to shape meaning.

steps.title: Openings
steps.body: How does the text begin? What effect does the opening have? - In media res (starting in the middle of the action) - Setting the scene - Creating mystery or intrigue

steps.title: Endings
steps.body: How does the text conclude? What is the final impression? - Resolution or closure - Cliffhanger or ambiguity - Reflective circular ending

steps.title: Narrative Perspective
steps.body: Who is telling the story? - First person (I, we) - personal, subjective - Third person (he, she, they) - more detached - Omniscient narrator - knows everything

steps.title: Try it yourself
steps.body: What is the difference between language and structure analysis? | Why might a writer use a short paragraph? | What does "in media res" mean?

steps.title: Check your answers
steps.body: Language analysis looks at word choice and literary devices; structure analysis looks at how the text is organised and sequenced. | To create impact, drama, tension, or to draw attention to a key moment or idea. | Starting in the middle of the action - a narrative technique that creates immediate engagement.

steps.title: Exam tips
steps.body: Trace the reader's journey through the text Comment on beginnings, middles and endings Look for shifts in focus, time, or perspective Use structural terminology: focus, shift, perspective, sequence Consider paragraph and sentence length Don't analyse language - that's a different question!
